lines.en: What separates a successful startup from a failing one is rarely the idea itself, but the way it is carried out.
Had the founders listened to their early customers, the company might have survived its first year.
It is believed that most new businesses fail within three years, mainly because they run out of cash.
Not only must an entrepreneur take risks, but they must also know which risks are worth taking.
However brilliant your product is, nobody will buy it if they have never heard of it.
The market is said to be changing so fast that last year's strategy may already be useless.
What investors really look for is not a perfect plan, but a team they can trust.
Were the company to lower its prices now, it would attract customers but lose their respect.
Little did he know that his small online shop would one day become a national brand.
It was her ability to adapt, not her original idea, that saved the business during the crisis.
What an investor finds most worrying is not a small loss, but a founder who refuses to admit mistakes.
Had the firm paid as much attention to its staff as to its profits, it might still be thriving.
It is far cheaper to keep an existing customer happy than to win a new one.
Not until the second year did the business make its first real profit.
However tempting a quick deal may be, a good reputation takes years to build and one day to lose.
